evidence.rejected_candidate_evidence_note: Rejected bundles keep full raw requests and responses under raw_evidence_dir; their scores and reasons are in candidate_rankings.

data.explanation: The oracle was derived from phase-j-intent v1 and locked ANC-001/002/008/012/013/014. It has 46 cases and 130 scored role cells: each approved pass and fail fixture plus compliant-paraphrase, silent, topical-only, conflict, irrelevant and exception/condition probes. ANC-001 is a prohibition, so only relevant and contradicted are scored, as in decide(). The oracle was frozen (sha256 f3b4bd117203fa882c7fdfd8affc71bb408f2bdda064ec4fe6d002c9d6f58749) and made read-only before the first Jev call, and no case was added or relabelled afterwards. 13 bundle evaluations (1196 Jev requests, 4 parallel evaluators, 0 errors, 0 retries) covered 5 relevant, 6 addressed and 8 contradicted candidates. The current set S0 scored 128/130 cells and 44/46 verdicts. It said addressed=yes on the silent ANC-008 pr_develop probe (a false satisfied at 0.6) and contradicted=yes on the ANC-014 topical-only probe. S5 (R0, A3, K5) was exact once, but its byte-identical replication S5b flipped A3 on ANC-008:silent, so it was rejected as unstable; a third call cannot vote it in. Sealed: S8 = current relevant (R0), condition-aware addressed (A5) and silence/exception-aware contradicted (K5). It was exact, stable and regression-free on 130/130 cells and 46/46 verdicts in each of three byte-identical runs (S8, S8b, S8c; 6 repeats per case). One set covers all six anchors because the result contract carries a single sealed set. History events 1-6 seal it per anchor (that anchor's oracle slice, score and run ids); event 7 is the bundle-level seal, whose authority.anchor_id field carries ANC-001 with all six anchor versions and the anchors-set digest because the schema allows a single anchor id. Production stays fail-closed at 0.6. With S8, these oracle cells remain below 0.6 in some or all repeats: ANC-001 exception_boundary (merge-wait exception, contradicted low; underspecified), ANC-012 topical_only and ANC-013 silent (relevant low; underspecified), ANC-002/ANC-014 fixture_pass (occasionally underspecified), and ANC-012/ANC-013 fixture_fail (contradicted yes but below 0.6, so production gives not_addressed: still failing). Every fixture_fail still fails and no known-bad probe passes in any repeat.
data.planner_action: Write the sealed question set (digest 86bc0e8bc63923adbbbe5bbbf68b0c559359c0a1b706c60d23d07655f0ac929b) with its canonical tuning history into the plan-questions record of ANC-001, ANC-002, ANC-008, ANC-012, ANC-013 and ANC-014, then re-run the planning gate on the formula steps. Do not lower the 0.6 production threshold. A step that stays underspecified is a plan-text matter: state the required content explicitly in that step, e.g. the literal `atm send omega-prime@hermes` at each decision point and escalation; for a BREAKING verdict, that the develop PR is left ready to merge and no PR to main is opened; and that the run waits on Rand only for his PR merges. A failure on these questions that you dispute goes to anchor-tuning triage, not to re-tuning.

criteria.no: The concrete requirement is absent from `item.text`, including when the item only mentions the same topic.
criteria.unclear: Part of `item.text` is garbled or missing, so presence cannot be judged.
criteria.yes: The concrete requirement appears in `item.text`, verbatim or paraphrased.

addressed.instructions: List to yourself the concrete requirement in `anchor.statement` (for example a recipient such as `omega-prime@hermes`, a command such as `atm send`, a limit on which files change, or a required end state such as a PR left ready to merge). Is that concrete requirement present in `item.text`? A paraphrase counts; a topic mention does not. When `anchor.statement` applies under a condition (for example when there are breaking changes, or when CI is green), the requirement is present only if `item.text` states what happens under that condition; doing a related step without addressing the condition does not count. Judge presence only, not conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only. Leaving a required step unmentioned, or marking a step done without saying what else happens, is silence, not contradiction. Anything `anchor.statement` itself names as allowed or as an exception is not a contradiction.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
